newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES SEND DYE, WALKER TO ROYALS FOR TUCKER, LOCKHART.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES SEND DYE, WALKER TO ROYALS FOR TUCKER, LOCKHART.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves followed up Tuesday's blockbuster deal with another trade Thursday, swapping outfielder Jermaine Dye for Michael Tucker in a four-player deal with the Kansas City Royals.
The Braves also sent minor league pitcher Jamie Walker to the Royals, who included infielder Keith Lockhart in the deal.

On Tuesday, Braves general manager John Schuerholz executed a blockbuster deal with the Cleveland Indians, acquiring outfielder Kenny Lofton and relief pitcher Alan Embree for outfielders Marquis Grissom and David Justice.

The 25-year-old Tucker hit .260 with 12 home runs and 53 RBI last season and was scheduled to be the Royals' starting right fielder in 1997. He missed the final month of the 1996 season after dislocating his left ring finger.
Lockhart, 32, hit .273 with seven homers and 55 RBI in 138 games last season.
The 23-year-old Dye made his major league debut in 1996 and hit .281 with 12 homers and 37 RBI in 92 games.

"Jermaine Dye is a classic right fielder and gives our club the right-handed power that we have been looking for," said Royals general manager Herk Robinson. "We think Jamie Walker will strengthen the left-handed pitching in the bullpen."

Walker, 25, pitched in the Houston organisation last season and was taken by the Royals in the Rule Five Draft in December. He was 5-1 with a 2.50 ERA at Jackson of the Double A Texas League last year.
The trade continues the reshaping of the Royals, who have added infielders Jay Bell and Jeff King and designated hitter Chili Davis to their starting lineup since the end of last season.
